speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of a swollen, painful left ankle that resolved on its own, combined with current right knee swelling and painful urination, is highly suggestive of crystal-induced arthritis. Did you notice that the joint fluid looked cloudy or yellowish when it was present, or have you experienced any fever or chills?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.
REQUEST TEST: Serum uric acid level.

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal urinalysis and serum uric acid levels, your history of a "cold" joint that resolved spontaneously followed by a painful urination episode and now a swollen knee strongly suggests gout, which can occasionally present with normal blood work during an acute flare. Have you noticed any redness or warmth over the affected joint, and do you have a history of kidney stones?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age, sexual activity with multiple partners, and inconsistent condom use, we must also consider a sexually transmitted infection like Reactive Arthritis or Gonococcal arthritis. Have you noticed any discharge from your urethra, and do you have a history of recent skin infections or eye redness? REQUEST TEST: NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea; REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's syndrome) secondary to prior Chlamydia infection. Although the NAAT was negative, the classic triad of arthritis, urethritis, and the history of prior STI risk, combined with the "cold" nature of the joint, strongly supports this diagnosis over gout or gonococcal arthritis. I recommend a trial of fluoroquinolone antibiotics and anti-inflammatory therapy.
